notes.front: What is My Library in the Service Trust Portal?
notes.back: A personal page where you save Service Trust Portal documents so the ones you care about sit in one place.
notes.explanation: It can also email you when Microsoft updates a saved document, so you need not keep checking the portal yourself.
notes.example: Like a bookmarks folder in a browser, but it can also tell you when a bookmarked report changes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “My Library”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Microsoft publish on the Service Trust Portal?
notes.back: Audit reports and other compliance information about its cloud services, plus whitepapers on how those services protect data.
notes.explanation: The portal is a public Microsoft site, and it also covers how you can manage cloud data security and compliance yourself.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Who produces the audit reports you can download from the Service Trust Portal?
notes.back: External auditors, not Microsoft.
notes.explanation: The portal distinguishes these independent reports from the whitepapers, which Microsoft writes itself.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which account must you sign in with to reach the Service Trust Portal resources that need authentication?
notes.back: Your Microsoft cloud services account: a Microsoft Entra organisation account.
notes.explanation: Only some resources are behind sign-in; the rest of the portal is public.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Accessing the Service Trust Portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Besides signing in, what must you accept before using some Service Trust Portal resources?
notes.back: The Microsoft Non-Disclosure Agreement for Compliance Materials.
notes.explanation: Microsoft’s get-started guide lists this agreement alongside the authenticated sign-in as a condition for those resources.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Get started with Microsoft Service Trust Portal, “Accessing the Service Trust Portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which online subscriptions give an existing customer access to the Service Trust Portal?
notes.back: Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 or Azure, whether trial or paid.
notes.explanation: Any one of the three is enough; new customers can sign up for a trial of one of them to get in.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Get started with Microsoft Service Trust Portal, “Existing customers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which roles let a user view restricted documents in the Service Trust Portal? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: Tenant Admin, Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Reader.
notes.explanation: Some documents are restricted because of what they contain, so the portal ties them to specific roles.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Get started with Microsoft Service Trust Portal, “Restricted Documents”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Service Trust Portal category holds security implementation and design information, arranged in tiles such as ISO/IEC, to help you meet regulatory compliance objectives?
notes.back: Certifications, Regulations, and Standards.
notes.explanation: Choosing a tile lists its documents, each with a description and the date it was last updated.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Certifications, Regulations, and Standards”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Service Trust Portal category holds general documents such as business continuity plans, third-party penetration test results and FAQs?
notes.back: Reports, Whitepapers, and Artifacts.
notes.explanation: It gathers documents that are not tied to one standard, industry or region.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Reports, Whitepapers, and Artifacts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Service Trust Portal category groups documents for particular sectors, such as healthcare, and for particular parts of the world?
notes.back: Industry and Regional Resources.
notes.explanation: Its documents are sorted by the industry or region they apply to rather than by standard.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Industry and Regional Resources”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Service Trust Portal category shows documents restricted to your tenant, based on your organisation’s subscription and permissions?
notes.back: Resources for your Organization.
notes.explanation: Unlike the other categories, what it shows depends on who you are signed in as.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Resources for your Organization”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the Service Trust Portal’s reports section, who carries out the penetration tests and security assessments that are attested there?
notes.back: Third parties.
notes.explanation: The Pen Test and Security Assessments group holds attestations of this outside testing.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Reports, Whitepapers, and Artifacts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which group of Service Trust Portal documents covers compliance, security and privacy for AI offerings such as Microsoft Copilot and Azure OpenAI?
notes.back: AI Resources, in Reports, Whitepapers, and Artifacts.
notes.explanation: Microsoft’s get-started guide lists it first among the general document groups.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Get started with Microsoft Service Trust Portal, “Reports, Whitepapers, and Artifacts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: For how long, at least, can you download a Service Trust Portal report after it is published?
notes.back: At least 12 months, or until a newer version replaces it.
notes.explanation: Documents with several versions show a series mark, and older versions can be viewed from the download page.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Get started with Microsoft Service Trust Portal, “Search”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Service Trust Portal industry group is kept exclusively for one kind of customer?
notes.back: United States Government: its resources are only for United States Government customers.
notes.explanation: It is the only industry group the training describes as exclusively for one kind of customer, so it answers a question of eligibility, not of topic.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Industry and Regional Resources”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Service Trust Portal industry group gives regulatory compliance guidance arranged by country or region?
notes.back: Financial Services.
notes.explanation: Its guidance is for financial services institutions and is sorted by where they operate.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Industry and Regional Resources”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How do you add a single Service Trust Portal document to My Library?
notes.back: Open the ellipsis (…) menu beside the document and choose Save to library.
notes.explanation: The get-started guide adds that you can tick several documents and save them together.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “My Library”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What can My Library’s notification settings do for you?
notes.back: Email an address in your organisation, at a frequency you choose, when Microsoft updates a document you saved.
notes.explanation: Each email links to the updated documents and briefly describes the change.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “My Library”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: You save a Service Trust Portal document that belongs to a series. What are you subscribed to?
notes.back: The whole series: you are notified when any update to that series appears.
notes.explanation: Saving one document of a series is treated as following the series.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “My Library”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Across which four areas does the Microsoft Trust Center set out Microsoft’s commitment to data privacy?
notes.back: Data control, data location, data security and data defence.
notes.explanation: Microsoft backs these areas with contractual commitments, and they shape how its products and services are designed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Microsoft's commitment to data privacy”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Under Microsoft’s “you control your data” principle, what can you do with your data?
notes.back: Access it, change it or delete it whenever you like; it belongs to you.
notes.explanation: Microsoft also commits not to use the data without your agreement.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “You control your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Once you agree to Microsoft using your data, what may Microsoft use it for?
notes.back: Only for providing the services you chose.
notes.explanation: It also rules out sharing the data with advertiser-supported services or mining it for advertising or marketing research.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “You control your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What limits apply to subcontractors that Microsoft lets reach your data?
notes.back: They may do only the work they were engaged for, under Microsoft’s own privacy commitments, and are audited beforehand.
notes.explanation: Authorised subprocessors are checked against strict security and privacy requirements before they start.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “You control your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which standard, described as the first international code of practice for cloud privacy, does Microsoft comply with to reinforce your control of your data?
notes.back: ISO/IEC 27018.
notes.explanation: Microsoft cites its compliance with broad privacy laws and standards such as this one as reinforcing the control principle.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “You control your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In which Microsoft cloud services does the privacy principle on data location say you can decide where your data is stored?
notes.back: Services such as Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365.
notes.explanation: Microsoft helps you pick the service and data location that suit your business.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Know where your data is located”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Why does Microsoft offer data residency options around the world?
notes.back: To help keep resiliency and compliance requirements within geographic boundaries.
notes.explanation: Microsoft backs the options with contractual commitments and openness about how data is stored and processed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Know where your data is located”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Microsoft guard against a single point of compromise when encrypting your data?
notes.back: With two or more independent encryption layers.
notes.explanation: If one layer were broken, another would still stand between an attacker and the data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Your data is secured at rest and in transit”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which two industry-standard protocols does Microsoft name for encrypting data in transit?
notes.back: Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Internet Protocol Security (IPsec).
notes.explanation: These are the examples Microsoft gives under the principle that your data is secured in transit.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Your data is secured at rest and in transit”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: The Microsoft Cloud offers encryption for data at rest up to {{c1::AES-256}}.
notes.back: AES-256
notes.explanation: The range of options lets you pick the encryption that best fits your business.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Your data is secured at rest and in transit”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Under the data security principle, which Azure service is named as giving you control over passwords, encryption keys and other secrets?
notes.back: Azure Key Vault.
notes.explanation: Microsoft-managed keys are secured by Microsoft; Key Vault is how you keep control of your own.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Your data is secured at rest and in transit”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where does Microsoft say government requests for your data should be sent?
notes.back: To you, the customer, not to Microsoft.
notes.explanation: Microsoft also says it gives no government direct or unfettered access to customer data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Microsoft defends your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: If a law enforcement agency demands your data from Microsoft, what does Microsoft do where the law allows?
notes.back: Tells you promptly, gives you a copy of the demand, and points the agency to you.
notes.explanation: It first checks that the demand is legally valid and appropriate, and discloses nothing except as you direct or the law requires.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Microsoft defends your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: For enterprise and public sector customers, what does Microsoft commit to do about government requests for their data?
notes.back: Challenge every such request where it can lawfully do so, in court if necessary.
notes.explanation: This defence of customer data is written into Microsoft’s contracts with those customers.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Microsoft defends your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An external auditor asks your firm for Microsoft’s ISO/IEC certification documents covering its cloud services. Where in the Service Trust Portal do you look first?
notes.back: A: Certifications, Regulations, and Standards.
notes.choices:
A) Certifications, Regulations, and Standards
B) Industry and Regional Resources
C) My Library
D) Resources for your Organization
notes.choicesExplained: B is sorted by sector and region, not by standard. C holds only documents you have already saved. D shows tenant-restricted documents for your organisation, not Microsoft’s standard certifications.
notes.explanation: Standards such as ISO/IEC appear as tiles in that category.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Certifications, Regulations, and Standards”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A compliance lead wants an email whenever Microsoft revises three particular Service Trust Portal reports. What should she use?
notes.back: C: save the reports to My Library and set up its notifications.
notes.choices:
A) Download the reports again every week
B) Search the portal and filter by date
C) Save the reports to My Library and set up its notifications
D) Ask for a restricted-documents role
notes.choicesExplained: A and B rely on her checking by hand. D controls which documents she may see, not whether she is told about updates.
notes.explanation: Notifications apply to documents saved in My Library.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “My Library”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A hospital group wants material on what Microsoft offers the health sector. Which Service Trust Portal category fits best?
notes.back: A: Industry and Regional Resources.
notes.choices:
A) Industry and Regional Resources
B) Resources for your Organization
C) Reports, Whitepapers, and Artifacts
D) Certifications, Regulations, and Standards
notes.choicesExplained: B is tied to your own tenant’s subscription and permissions. C holds general documents that are not sector-specific. D is arranged by standard, not by industry.
notes.explanation: Healthcare and Life Sciences is one of the industry groups in that category.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Industry and Regional Resources”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A customer asks what happens if a foreign authority demands its mailbox data from Microsoft. Which of Microsoft’s privacy principles answers this?
notes.back: D: Microsoft defends your data.
notes.choices:
A) You control your data
B) Know where your data is located
C) Your data is secured at rest and in transit
D) Microsoft defends your data
notes.choicesExplained: A is about your right to use, change and delete data and limits on Microsoft’s use. B is about choosing where data is stored. C is about encryption.
notes.explanation: That principle covers how Microsoft handles government and law enforcement requests.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Microsoft defends your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A regulator requires that a company’s customer records stay in its own country. Which Microsoft privacy principle speaks to this?
notes.back: B: Know where your data is located.
notes.choices:
A) You control your data
B) Know where your data is located
C) Your data is secured at rest and in transit
D) Microsoft defends your data
notes.choicesExplained: A covers access, deletion and Microsoft’s use of data, not its location. C covers encryption. D covers responses to government requests.
notes.explanation: That principle lets you choose where data is stored and offers data residency options within geographic boundaries.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Know where your data is located”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Microsoft privacy principle includes the use of TLS between a user’s browser and Microsoft 365?
notes.back: C: Your data is secured at rest and in transit.
notes.choices:
A) Know where your data is located
B) Microsoft defends your data
C) Your data is secured at rest and in transit
D) You control your data
notes.choicesExplained: A is about storage location. B is about government requests. D is about your rights over the data and Microsoft’s limited use of it.
notes.explanation: TLS is one of the transport protocols named under that principle.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “Your data is secured at rest and in transit”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A consultant browsing the Service Trust Portal without signing in finds that some documents will not open for him. What does he most likely need?
notes.back: D: to sign in with a Microsoft Entra organisation account.
notes.choices:
A) To change the portal language
B) To save the documents to My Library first
C) To buy a separate Service Trust Portal licence
D) To sign in with a Microsoft Entra organisation account
notes.choicesExplained: A changes only the display language. B only gathers documents in one place; it does not unlock them. C: access comes with a Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 or Azure subscription, trial or paid, not a separate portal licence.
notes.explanation: Some portal resources are open only to authenticated users of Microsoft cloud services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the offerings of the Service Trust portal, “Accessing the Service Trust Portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A customer is assured that Microsoft will not mine its cloud data for advertising. Which Microsoft privacy principle gives that assurance?
notes.back: B: You control your data.
notes.choices:
A) Microsoft defends your data
B) You control your data
C) Know where your data is located
D) Your data is secured at rest and in transit
notes.choicesExplained: A covers government and law enforcement requests. C covers where data is stored. D covers encryption.
notes.explanation: That principle limits Microsoft to using your data only for the services you chose.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft's privacy principles, “You control your data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
